findings.title: International transfer information is not clearly UK-specific
findings.detail: The policy says personal data may be transferred outside the European Economic Area and refers generally to appropriate safeguards, but does not identify the relevant UK transfer mechanism or clearly explain transfers outside the UK.

findings.reasoning: UK GDPR transparency requires information about relevant international transfers and safeguards. The policy gives some general information, so this is assessed as medium rather than high; the evidence does not establish that a transfer itself was unlawful.

letter.subject: Concerns about tracking and cookie practices following rejection of cookies on rolls-royce.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://rolls-royce.com on 2026-11-08 04:07 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit detected the cookie banner, clicked the reject option (“DECLINE COOKIES”), then visited pages on products and services, innovation, and sustainability, while recording what was still sent.

The main points are as follows.

1. After cookies were rejected, three requests were still sent to facebook.net. These were classified as advertising requests.

2. Our review suggests this continued Facebook advertising activity after rejection may conflict with the site statement in the privacy policy that information “will not be used in ways to which you have not consented.”

3. Scripts from equally.ai at https://widget.prod.equally.ai/equally-widget.min.js used audio, canvas and WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting before any cookie choice was made and again after cookies were rejected.

4. Our review suggests that this fingerprinting may also conflict with the site’s consent wording. The cookie policy states: “A cookie is a small file of letters and numbers that we store on your browser or the hard drive of your computer, smart phone, tablet or other electronic device if you agree.”

5. We reviewed the privacy policy at https://www.rolls-royce.com/site-services/data-privacy.aspx. It names 0 companies. During the audit, Facebook was observed, and we found no mention of Facebook in the policy.

6. Our review suggests the privacy policy does not clearly identify the UK GDPR lawful basis for each relevant processing purpose, including advertising and analytics.

7. Our review also suggests the policy’s international transfer information is not clearly UK-specific. It refers to transfers outside the EEA and general safeguards, but does not clearly explain the relevant UK position.

Please would you:

1. Explain each of the points above.
2. Confirm which cookies, trackers or other technologies you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential tracking or similar technologies operating without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter cannot be resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
